seoTitle: How to Make TradingView Full Screen Easily
metaDescription: Learn how to switch TradingView into full screen mode using keyboard shortcuts or UI options, hide panels and toolbars, and maximize chart space.
intro: A cramped chart makes technical analysis harder than it needs to be, and TradingView offers several ways to maximize your chart space. This guide covers enabling full screen mode, using keyboard shortcuts, and hiding panels for a distraction-free layout.

steps.heading: Enable full screen mode
steps.body: Look for the full screen icon on your TradingView chart toolbar to expand the chart to fill your browser window.

steps.heading: Use keyboard shortcuts
steps.body: TradingView supports keyboard shortcuts for instantly toggling full screen mode without hunting through menus.

steps.heading: Hide panels, toolbars, and sidebars
steps.body: Turn off watchlists, the drawing toolbar, and other side panels individually to free up even more chart space.

steps.heading: Set up a clean layout
steps.body: Combine full screen mode with hidden panels to create a minimal, distraction-free view suited for focused analysis.

steps.heading: Exit full screen when needed
steps.body: Use the same toggle or shortcut to return to the normal view and restore your panels and toolbars.

faq.question: Does full screen mode work in the TradingView mobile app?
faq.answer: Full screen behaves differently on mobile, generally by rotating the device or tapping the chart to hide the surrounding app interface.

faq.question: Is there a keyboard shortcut for full screen in TradingView?
faq.answer: Yes, TradingView supports a dedicated shortcut to toggle full screen instantly on desktop and browser.

faq.question: Can I save a full screen layout as default?
faq.answer: TradingView doesn't force full screen as a startup default, but you can quickly re-enable it each session with the shortcut or toolbar icon.

faq.question: Why does my chart look the same after entering full screen?
faq.answer: If panels like the watchlist or toolbar are still open, hide them individually since full screen mode alone doesn't remove all UI elements.
